b1-adj-fest: In winter the lake ice is hard enough to walk on. It is no longer liquid. Which adjective describes it?
The teacher says the date of the exam is decided and will not change.
You hold the rope tightly and nothing can pull it out of your hands. Your grip is strong and does not give way.
b1-v-besetzen: You put your jacket on a train seat so nobody else can sit there. What are you doing to the seat?
A company needs to find someone for its empty manager position. What must it do with the job?
The hospital needs enough nurses so the night shift has people at every desk. Which verb means 'to man' or 'to staff'?
b1-n-u-bahn: In Berlin you go down the stairs into a station below the street, and a train arrives in a tunnel.
You want to avoid the traffic jams in the big city, so you take the train that runs under the ground.
London has the 'Tube' and New York has the 'Subway'. Which noun means this kind of train?
b1-n-asyl: A woman from a country in danger arrives in Germany and asks for protection and a safe place to live.
A man has to leave his home country and applies for official protection in another country.
Which noun means the protection a country gives to people who flee from danger?
b1-n-migration: Every autumn birds fly in large groups to warmer countries and return in spring. Which noun names this movement?
Many people move from the countryside to big cities to find work.
The news reports that many people leave one country to settle in another.
b1-v-festlegen: You and your landlord write exactly how much the rent will be in the contract. The amount is now decided.
The manager writes down the rules for the team: how long each break lasts.
The class agrees on a date for the trip, and everyone says it is final.
b1-n-schwangerschaft: Your sister is expecting a baby, and the doctor says it takes about nine months.
A woman at work tells her boss she is expecting a child and will go on leave later.
In the pharmacy you buy a test to find out if a woman is going to have a baby.
b1-adv-kuerzlich: A friend asks if you have seen a good film lately. You say you saw one just a few days ago.
You met your neighbor not long ago, and he told you he was moving.
You say you started your new job only a short time ago. Which adverb means 'recently'?
b1-adj-ausgezeichnet: You taste the soup and it is the best you ever had. You tell the cook it is perfect.
A teacher reads your essay and gives you the best possible grade for superb work.
At the hotel the service was so good that you write a review with the highest praise.
b1-n-angabe: On a form you must write your name, address and date of birth. These details are required.
The police ask you to tell them what you saw. What you tell them is recorded.
The label on the box shows the size and weight of the product. These facts are printed there.
b1-v-garantieren: The seller promises that if the phone breaks within two years, he will fix it for free.
The airline says you will get your money back for sure if your flight is cancelled.
Your friend says: 'I promise one hundred percent that I will be there at eight.'
b1-n-etage: In a block of flats you live on the third level above the ground floor, and you take the lift.
In the department store a sign says the toys are on the second level.
A hotel receptionist says: 'Your room is on the fifth level.' Which noun means 'floor' in a building?
b1-n-ursache: The firefighters study why the fire started. They look for what made it happen.
The doctor wants to know what made you sick, so he asks about your food and your travels.
The train is late, and the announcer explains the reason: a fault with a signal.
b1-adj-gering: The shop has only a tiny number of apples left. The amount is very small.
The doctor says the risk is very low, so you need not worry.
The difference in price between the two phones is only slight, just two euros.
b1-n-integration: A new family from abroad learns the language, goes to the local school and makes friends. They become part of the community.
The city offers language courses to help newcomers become part of society.
Which noun means the process of becoming a full part of a group or society?
b1-v-kleben: A stamp must be put on the envelope with a bit of gum.
Your child makes a paper picture and attaches little pieces with paste.
The sticker will not come off. It stays on the window. Which verb means 'to stick'?
b1-n-knopf: Your jacket has small round pieces that go through holes to close it, and one has fallen off.
To call the lift you push a round thing on the wall.
The radio has a round thing you turn to make the sound louder.
b1-n-notaufnahme: A boy breaks his arm at night. His parents drive to the part of the hospital that is open all day and night for urgent cases.
Your friend has strong chest pain on Sunday and no doctor's office is open, so you go to a special hospital department.
A hospital sign says: 'Open day and night for serious accidents.'
b1-v-kaputtmachen: A toddler pulls the toy so hard that it is ruined. You say: 'You have ruined it!'
Your brother dropped your phone, and now it does not work anymore.
You step on your glasses by accident, and they are in pieces.
b1-n-schreck: You hear a sudden loud bang behind you and your heart jumps.
Your friend jumps out from behind the door and you get a big scare.
You think you have lost your wallet, and a sudden feeling of fear goes through you.
b1-adj-original: The museum shows the real painting by the artist, not a copy.
A shop sells genuine brand shoes, not fake ones.
You watch a film in the language it was first made in, not dubbed.
b1-n-besprechung: At ten o'clock all colleagues sit around a table in the office to talk about the project.
Your boss says: 'I cannot talk now, I am in a work discussion with the team.'
A teacher and a parent sit down to talk about a child's progress at a planned time.
b1-v-verschwinden: You look for your keys on the table, but they are gone, and nobody knows where.
The magician puts a coin in his hand, opens it, and the coin is no longer there.
At sunrise the fog slowly goes away until nothing is left of it.
b1-n-ehe: Your grandparents have been husband and wife for fifty years.
At the wedding the priest talks about the lifelong bond between two partners.
Which noun means the legal union of a husband and wife?
b1-adv-andererseits: You think about a new job: the pay is better, but the way to work is longer. Which word introduces the second, opposite point?
A friend talks about a holiday abroad: sunny and cheap, but the flight is long. Which adverb starts the contrasting side?
You give two sides of an argument. Which word means 'on the other hand'?
b1-n-notausgang: In the cinema a green sign with a running person shows the door to use if there is a fire.
On a plane the flight attendant shows you the doors for use in case of danger.
The back door of a shop must not be blocked, because people need it in case of danger.
b1-n-visitenkarte: At a trade fair you give a stranger a small paper with your name, job and phone number.
After the meeting the manager hands you a small card with her company's logo and email.
On your desk you keep small cards from many business contacts in a holder.
b1-v-treiben: A leaf falls into the river and is carried slowly along by the water.
The shepherd moves the cows along the road to the meadow.
The boat lost its engine and moves aimlessly with the waves.
b1-adj-interkulturell: A workshop at the company shows how people from different cultures can work well together.
Your school has a project where students from many countries cook food from their homelands.
Friends from Turkey, Brazil and Germany talk about differences in customs. Which adjective describes this exchange between cultures?
b1-n-alkohol: At the party the driver says: 'No beer or wine for me, I have to drive.'
The label on the bottle says it contains 40 percent of the thing that makes people drunk.
In the pharmacy a clear liquid for cleaning wounds contains this.
b1-n-fluessigkeit: The doctor says you should drink lots of water and tea. What you take in each day is called what?
Water, oil and milk are not solid and not gas. They flow.
A bottle has leaked, and something wet runs onto the floor.
b1-v-vermissen: You live far from your family and feel sad because they are not near you.
Your friend moved abroad. You think of him often and wish he were here.
A child at camp feels sad because he wants to go home to his parents.
b1-n-krieg: In history class you learn about the fighting between countries that lasted from 1939 to 1945.
The news shows a country where armies are fighting and people leave their homes.
Which noun is the opposite of peace?
b1-adj-oestlich: The sun rises in this direction, so you look to this side in the morning.
Poland lies in this direction from Germany, and so does the sunrise.
On the map you go from Berlin toward the side where the sun rises. Which adjective means 'east'?
b1-n-stimme: On the phone you hear a woman with a deep, warm sound and recognize your aunt.
On election day each citizen can put one mark on the paper for a favorite candidate.
You have a cold and can hardly speak because the sound in your throat is gone.
b1-v-erfordern: This job needs a lot of patience and years of training.
Learning a language takes time and daily effort.
Repairing the old clock calls for great care. Which verb means 'to require'?
b1-n-fabrik: Hundreds of workers make cars on assembly lines in a large building.
The chocolate you buy was made in a big building full of machines.
Your uncle works in a big plant at the edge of town that produces shoes.
b1-n-fasching: In February people wear costumes and masks, and parades go down the street with music.
Children go to school dressed as pirates and princesses before the time of fasting.
Cologne and Munich have colorful parties with costumes. Which noun means 'carnival'?
b1-n-statistik: The news shows a chart with numbers about how many people had a job in each year.
A student collects numbers about her class and calculates averages and percentages.
After the football match a table shows numbers of goals, passes and shots.
b1-adv-inzwischen: You cook pasta and say that while it boils you will make the sauce.
You have not seen your friend for five years, and he is a father now.
You waited for an hour, and during that time your friend had called three times.
b1-v-mischen: You pour blue and yellow paint into a bowl and stir it, and it becomes green.
At the card table you shuffle the cards before dealing.
The bartender puts juice and water into one glass.
b1-adj-vorlaeufig: The dentist gives you a tooth to wear for a few weeks until the final one is ready.
The first results of the election are not final yet.
You get a short-term pass for the first week until your real card arrives.
b1-n-gegensatz: Hot and cold, big and small. Each pair shows two things that are completely different.
Two brothers are totally unlike: one is tidy and the other messy. What is the relation between them?
Which noun means the 'opposite' of something?
b1-n-abschied: At the airport you hug your friend and say goodbye for a long time.
At the retirement party colleagues give gifts and speeches as the old boss leaves.
The train starts moving and everyone waves. It is a sad parting.
b1-v-faulenzen: It is Sunday, and you stay on the sofa all day and do nothing.
On holiday you lie on the beach and do absolutely nothing, with no plans.
Your teenage brother lies around instead of helping with the chores.
b1-n-nichtraucher: In the restaurant a man asks for a table in the area where smoking is not allowed, since he never smokes.
On a train a sign says one coach is reserved for people who do not smoke.
A man says he has never smoked in his life. What is he?
b1-n-waschmittel: You fill the washing machine with clothes and then pour powder or liquid into the drawer.
In the supermarket you buy a big box so your shirts smell fresh.
You run out of the stuff that makes your laundry clean.
b1-adj-muendlich: The language exam has two parts: one written, and one where you speak with the examiner.
A contract was only agreed by speaking, and nothing is written down.
The teacher gives you a grade for speaking in class.
b1-n-industrie: Germany has many companies producing cars and machines. This whole area of the economy is called what?
The mayor wants new factories in town to create jobs in the production sector.
Car making employs millions of people around the world, as part of this sector.
b1-v-einfuehren: The company starts using a new software system next month.
A shop brings goods from other countries into the country to sell them.
A new law will begin to apply next year, and the government is putting it in place.
b1-n-holz: A carpenter makes a table from the material that comes from trees.
In winter you put pieces of the material from trees into the fireplace.
The old floor of the house is made of this material. Which noun means 'wood'?
b1-n-einrichtung: A school, a hospital and a library are public places run by the city.
You look at the new apartment: the sofa, tables and shelves, everything that is in the rooms.
The sports center offers a pool and a gym on its premises.
b1-v-berechnen: The garage says they will ask you to pay 80 euros for the repair.
A student uses a calculator to work out the area of a circle.
The shopkeeper adds up all the prices to find the total cost.
b1-adj-zugaenglich: The museum has ramps and lifts, so people in wheelchairs can enter.
The library's old books are open to everybody, and anyone can use them.
The new boss is friendly and easy to talk to, so you can approach him.
b1-n-briefumschlag: You write a letter, then put it in a paper cover and stick on a stamp.
For the wedding you put money and a card into a small paper cover.
The post office sells you a paper cover big enough for A4 documents.
b1-n-intelligenz: A test measures how clever you are with logic puzzles.
A scientist says computers can imitate human thinking, and calls this 'artificial'.
Your dog learned the trick in minutes, and people praise its cleverness.
b1-adv-ueberhaupt: You ask if your friend likes cooking. He says he cannot cook, not even a little bit.
You ask a stranger: 'Do you speak English at all?'
You ask: 'Where do you actually come from, anyway?'
b1-v-operieren: The doctor says your appendix must be removed, and she will cut you open in the hospital tomorrow.
The surgeon is in the operating room with a mask and the patient.
A vet fixes a dog's broken leg with a small procedure.
b1-n-unterstuetzung: Your parents give you money and encouragement while you study.
A neighbor helps you carry boxes when you move, and you thank him for it.
The fans cheer loudly for their team at every match.
b1-n-streichholz: To light the candle you rub a small wooden stick on the side of a little box.
On a camping trip you need a little stick that makes fire to start the campfire.
A box holds forty tiny sticks with red tips.
b1-adj-unglaublich: You tell your friend you won a free trip to Hawaii, and he can hardly believe it.
The magician makes an elephant disappear, and the audience cannot believe what they see.
Which adjective describes something so surprising that it is hard to believe?
b1-n-hausmeister: In your block of flats a man fixes broken lights and sweeps the stairs.
At school a man opens the building in the morning and repairs the doors.
The heating is off, so you call the man who looks after the building.
b1-v-brennen: On the table a candle is lit and its flame gives light.
The wood in the fireplace is on fire and gives off heat.
The house is on fire and fire trucks arrive.
b1-n-talent: A six-year-old plays the piano beautifully without much practice. He has a natural gift.
Your friend draws amazing portraits without lessons. She has a special gift.
A TV show searches for singers and dancers who have special natural skills.
b1-n-beziehung: Anna and Paul have been a couple for three years, and they love each other.
You and your boss get along well. This is how two people are connected.
Studies find a link between smoking and cancer. This connection is called what?
b1-v-beleidigen: A driver shouts rude names at you from his car, and you feel hurt.
You said your friend's cooking was awful, and now he is offended.
At school one boy calls another one a stupid name.
b1-n-knoedel: In a Bavarian restaurant your roast pork comes with a big round ball made of potato or bread.
Your grandmother cooks round balls of dough in boiling water and serves them with gravy.
A cookbook for traditional German food shows round balls of potato dough steamed in water.
b1-adj-suedlich: Italy lies in this direction from Germany, toward the warm midday sun.
The part of the country toward this direction is warmer.
You drive from Hamburg toward the Alps, in this direction. Which adjective means 'south'?
b1-n-unterlagen: At the bank you must bring papers like your passport, contract and salary slips.
The lawyer asks you to bring all your files for the meeting.
You apply for a job, and the company sends a list of papers to send, like your CV and certificates.
b1-n-raucher: A man stands outside the restaurant in the cold and lights a cigarette every hour.
The doctor asks: 'You cough a lot. Do you smoke?' The man says yes, for twenty years. What is he?
At work a colleague takes a break five times a day to smoke.
b1-v-tauschen: Two children give each other stickers: you give me yours and I give you mine.
You do not like your seat on the plane, so you ask your neighbor to change places with you.
After the match two football players give each other their shirts.
b1-n-zweck: You ask what a strange tool is for: 'What is the point of this device?'
The form asks for what reason you are visiting the country: tourism or business.
Spending hours on this has no use, and the aim is unclear.
b1-adj-locker: The screw on the chair is not tight, and the chair wobbles.
Your new boss is calm and easy-going and does not mind small mistakes.
The rope is not tight and hangs down slack.
b1-adv-nun: After a long wait the teacher says: 'We begin the test at this moment.'
You have heard all the arguments and ask: 'Well, what do we do at this point?'
At the start of a speech the speaker says: 'And so, at this moment, let me begin.'
b1-n-region: The tourist office says Bavaria is a beautiful part of Germany with its own customs.
You come from a wine-growing part of the country, not from a city.
The weather forecast is for the northern part of the country.
b1-v-beeinflussen: Advertising can change what people buy without them noticing.
Rain has an effect on your mood, and you feel sleepy.
Your friends have an effect on what music you like.
b1-n-literatur: At university you study novels, poems and plays from many centuries.
A famous prize is given for the best writing in novels and poems.
In the library there is a section with books by famous writers.
b1-n-kriminalpolizei: After a burglary, detectives in plain clothes, not the officers in uniform on the street, arrive to investigate.
On TV the investigators who solve serious crimes work for this part of the police.
Which noun means the police unit that investigates serious crimes?
b1-v-ergaenzen: In the recipe you say 'also add a little salt' to finish it.
Your friend gave an answer, and you add one more detail that was missing.
You fill in the missing words in a sentence to make it complete.
b1-n-sieg: Your team scored three goals and the other team scored one, so you won the game.
The athlete crosses the finish line first and raises her arms.
The chess club celebrates winning the tournament. Which noun means 'victory'?
b1-adj-vegetarisch: At the restaurant a dish without meat or fish is marked on the menu with a green leaf.
Your friend never eats meat or fish, only vegetables, cheese and eggs.
A burger is made only of beans and vegetables. Which adjective describes it?
b1-n-muenze: The parking machine accepts only metal pieces, no paper money.
A child collects round metal pieces of money from many countries.
You flip it to decide: heads or tails.
b1-n-leistung: The teacher praises your excellent work in the exam: 'Great result!'
The electric motor produces 100 kilowatts. What is this measure of strength called?
The hotel offers breakfast and parking as part of the price. These things are what you get.
b1-v-darstellen: A painter paints a picture that shows a village in winter.
An actor plays the role of a king in the theatre.
The graph shows how sales grew over the year.
b1-n-vermittlung: A conflict between two neighbors is solved by a third person who talks to both sides.
You pay an agency a fee for finding a flat for you.
The job center sets up a job for you.
b1-adj-staedtisch: The swimming pool belongs to the city, not to a private company.
A person who grew up in a big town has this way of life, not a rural one.
The tourist says life in the country is quiet, but the life in the city is busy. Which adjective is about the city?
b1-n-dieb: Someone steals your wallet from your bag on the bus and runs away.
A man takes bread from a shop without paying.
The police are looking for the man who got into the house at night and took jewelry.
b1-v-trocknen: You wash your hair and then use a towel so it is no longer wet.
After washing, you hang the clothes on the line in the sun.
The dishes are wet, so you wipe them with a cloth.
b1-n-pflaster: You cut your finger, so you put a small sticky strip over the cut.
The street in the old town is covered with small stones.
At the pharmacy you ask for a box of sticky strips for small wounds.
b1-adv-runter: Your friend is on the roof, and you tell him to come toward the ground. Which adverb means 'down'?
A child is in a tree, and you say: 'Get ___ from there!' Which small word means 'down'?
On the escalator you move in the direction of the lower floor.
b1-n-honig: Bees make a sweet, golden, sticky food that you spread on bread.
With a cold you stir a spoon of a sweet, sticky food made by bees into your tea.
At the farmers' market you buy a jar of the sweet golden food made by bees.
b1-n-fernsehen: In the evening your family watches news, films and shows on a screen.
Your grandfather says: 'In the old days we only had radio, but now we have moving pictures at home.'
You work for a company that broadcasts shows and news to screens.
b1-v-entgegenkommen: You walk toward your friend, who walks along the same street from the other side, and you meet.
A car drives toward you on a narrow road.
The shop agrees to lower the price a bit to meet you halfway.
b1-adj-kreativ: Your friend invents original ideas, writes songs and paints pictures.
A designer finds an unusual new solution for the poster.
The teacher wants new ideas, not copying. Which adjective describes such a person?
b1-n-einbruch: Last night someone got into the neighbors' flat through the window and took the TV.
The shop's sales dropped suddenly by half this month.
The police warn that the number of burglaries goes up in winter, when people enter homes to steal.
b1-n-fall: Detectives are working on a difficult police investigation, a mystery to solve.
The patient's situation: 'In this situation we must call the doctor.'
A glass slips off the table and moves down onto the floor.
b1-v-sinken: A stone thrown into a pond goes down to the bottom.
The price of fuel goes down this month.
The temperature at night drops below zero.
b1-n-dialog: In an English book two people talk back and forth, written line by line.
A play in which two actors speak with each other.
The teacher asks you to practice a conversation between two people in class.
b1-n-umwelt: You sort your garbage and use a bicycle so as not to harm the nature, air and water around us.
The factory pollutes the river, and people say it harms the natural world.
In a lesson about protecting nature, which noun means the world around us?
b1-adj-absolut: Your friend says he is a hundred percent sure and has no doubt. Which adjective describes this?
At night in the forest there is complete silence, not a sound.
You say that you have total trust in your sister.
